concepts.label: Distributed ACID Transactions
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - this is the JUDGMENT CALL the round-12 brief asked for. This page is neither n1ql:transactions nor sdk:distributed-transaction alone: it explicitly treats KV operations (via SDK) and Query DML statements (via SQL++) as two interchangeable surfaces onto ONE mechanism ('Seamless integration between Key-Value (KV) and Query DML statements... within transactions'; 'Multiple Key-Value and Query DML statements can be used together inside a transaction'), and it describes the shared internal mechanics (Active Transaction Records, staged XATTR mutations, cleanup, atomic-commit-point) that underlie BOTH surfaces, never picking one over the other. That is exactly server:distributed-acid-transactions's existing definition: 'the server-side transaction feature that both SQL++ transaction statements and the SDK transaction APIs are surfaces onto.' This page is that concept's own canonical 'learn/' account - not a fourth thing.

concepts.label: Active Transaction Record (ATR)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - new namespace 'txn:' per the round-12 brief, for transaction internals not already covered by n1ql:*/sdk:*. The metadata document (prefix `_txn:atr-`) that tracks per-attempt commit state; the single point of truth an 'atomic commit' switches.

concepts.label: staged mutation
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the mechanism by which an in-transaction document change is written to the document's extended attributes (XATTRs) rather than its body, keeping it invisible until commit. Does not itself model XATTRs as a concept - see extended-attributes-fundamentals.md, covered by a sibling agent this round.

concepts.label: transaction cleanup process
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the asynchronous background process, started with the `Transactions` object, that scans for and resolves expired/abandoned staged changes across all buckets.

concepts.label: custom metadata collection
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the configurable alternative to the default per-bucket ATR storage location, set via `TransactionConfigBuilder.metadataCollection(...)`.

concepts.label: transaction expiry timer
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the configurable duration (default 15 seconds) after which an in-progress transaction is rolled back.

concepts.label: delta table
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the in-memory structure that grows with every mutation inside a (non-single-query) transaction, the stated reason to limit mutation count per transaction.

concepts.label: transaction isolation level (Read Committed + Monotonic Atomic View)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the fixed (non-configurable) isolation guarantee: stricter than plain Read Committed because of the added Monotonic Atomic View property.

concepts.label: kvtimeout (transaction setting)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - sibling of the already-promoted n1ql:txid/n1ql:tximplicit named-parameter concepts; the maximum wait time for a KV operation inside a transaction, default 2.5s.

concepts.label: atrcollection (transaction setting)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - sibling of n1ql:txid/n1ql:tximplicit; names the collection where ATRs and client records are stored.

concepts.label: Administrative (classic RBAC role category)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a NEW, deliberately separate sibling of role:full-administrator/role:eventing-full-admin/role:local-user-security-administrator/role:query-external-access (the classic cluster-wide RBAC family). Minted a dedicated predicate (requiresRbacRoleCategory) rather than reusing Sync Gateway's requiresRole, precisely because this ontology already tracks 'role' as a five-way collision and this page names broad role CATEGORIES, not the sync-function role check or a Capella role.

concepts.label: Data (classic RBAC role category)

concepts.label: Query & Index (classic RBAC role category)

concepts.label: Cross Data Center Replication (XDCR) - server-side replication feature

notable_absence.finding: No version is cited anywhere on this page for any part of the transaction feature - not for distributed transactions generally, not for statement-level atomicity, not for single query transactions/tximplicit, not for custom metadata collections. This is a major, clearly evolved feature (the settings table alone lists 6 independently-configurable parameters) with zero dating, consistent with round 12's genre finding that conceptual pages trade version/privilege facts for taxonomy - but the gap is unusually large here given the feature's evident maturity and complexity.

cross_component_finding: Two deliberate non-merges recorded here, following the ontology's established discipline: (1) server:xdcr (this page's sense - the general server-side replication feature) is kept separate from the already-promoted capella:xdcr ('a monitored Capella component, explicitly NOT one of the Services') - same acronym, different scope, no page states equivalence. (2) role:administrative-rbac-category/data-rbac-category/query-and-index-rbac-category are new siblings in the role: namespace's classic-cluster-RBAC family, but are related to server:distributed-acid-transactions via a freshly minted requiresRbacRoleCategory rather than the existing requiresRole (Sync Gateway's requireRole() check) or requiresCapellaRole (Capella management-plane roles) - a sixth data point for the ontology's now well-documented multi-way 'role' collision, deliberately not merged into any of the other five. Separately, this page is the strongest evidence yet that durability:durable-write (minted in durability.json, this same batch) and sdk:transaction-durability (already promoted) are genuinely different things at different scopes: this page cites the general 3-level enum as a transaction property in its own right (Durability ACID paragraph) AND separately delegates actual configuration to the Java-SDK-specific promoted concept (settings table) - two facts, two relations, not collapsed into one.
cross_product_finding: This single Server-tree conceptual page is a genuine cross-product hub: it links out to all nine language-specific SDK 'Distributed ACID Transactions' how-to pages (C++, .NET, Go, Java, Kotlin, Node.js, PHP, Python, Scala) plus the SQL++ statement reference plus XDCR/replication docs plus RBAC/roles plus install/NTP docs - more distinct product-area fan-out from one page than almost anything else extracted so far in the corpus. It is also the page that most directly justifies server:distributed-acid-transactions's own registry description ('the server-side transaction feature that both SQL++ transaction statements and the SDK transaction APIs are surfaces onto') - this extraction is the first to actually read that unifying page rather than one of its surfaces.
